mainTopic: When a כהן or a witness is believed about a בכור's blemish: hearsay, הפה שאסר, מה לו לשקר, and things that can easily come out
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: רבי מאיר suspects כהנים of blemishing a בכור only as a worry, not as a proven fact. Next the גמרא asks whether עד מפי עד (hearsay) is valid for a בכור. It concludes that it is, based on רב אשי's rereading of the ברייתא of the school of מנשה. רבי אילעא then rules that a person is believed when he says an animal is a בכור and that its blemish came by itself. The גמרא defends this ruling with the idea that a cheater would have made an obvious blemish. It also shows that 'מה לו לשקר' works against a mere suspicion, even though it does not work against witnesses. A dramatic story follows: רבי צדוק's question about a חבר versus an עם הארץ leads רבן גמליאל to publicly confront רבי יהושע, until the people stop the lecture. Finally, a new משנה trusts a כהן who says an expert saw his בכור. רב adds that a כהן is believed that a ישראל gave him the animal already blemished, because people do not lie about what can easily come out. רב שיזבי challenges that rule, and the answer begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next one.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's suspicion is only a precaution
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers a question left over from the earlier discussion. When רבי מאיר called כהנים suspect, he only meant there is a worry, not that they are proven to cause blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say that רבי מאיר spoke only about a worry. Did he ever say we should treat them as people who definitely do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion. It explains that רבי מאיר's suspicion of כהנים is only a precaution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference between worrying that someone might have done something wrong and declaring that he did it. רבי מאיר only said the first. So we cannot draw the harsher results that would follow from treating כהנים as people who are known to cause blemishes.

keyTerms.meaning: A concern or worry, a reason to be careful
To treat them as established, as proven to be that way
The תנא who holds that כהנים are suspect about blemishing a בכור
Say, you can say (a word that opens an answer)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying רבי מאיר trusts כהנים. He still suspects them; he just does not treat them as people known to cause blemishes.

phrases.english: Say that Rabbi Meir said it only for a concern;
phrases.notes: He means רבי מאיר's ruling that כהנים are suspect of causing blemishes, from the earlier discussion.

phrases.english: did he say it to establish them as definitely doing it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question raised on the previous daf about רבי מאיר's view
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of רבי מאיר's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר treats כהנים as people known to blemish animals
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר only holds there is a worry, which is a precaution and not a proven fact

steps.title: Is hearsay testimony valid for a firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: can a witness who only heard about the blemish from another witness testify that a בכור has a מום?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the law of a witness repeating what another witness told him, when the testimony is about a בכור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a question. It asks whether hearsay testimony counts for a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a witness has to testify about what he saw himself. The question is whether the rules for a בכור are looser, so that second-hand testimony about how the blemish came about would be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (the opening of a real open question)
A witness speaking from the mouth of another witness, meaning hearsay testimony
Testimony about a firstborn animal's blemish

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
a witness speaking from the mouth of a witness,
what is the law for testimony about a firstborn?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion ends
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether hearsay testimony is accepted about a בכור's blemish

steps.title: רב אסי forbids, רב אשי permits
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים disagree. רב אסי does not accept hearsay for a בכור, and רב אשי does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי forbids it, and רב אשי permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the two opinions on the question. It is setting up the argument between them that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי holds the normal rule: hearsay is not enough, so the בכור may not be slaughtered. רב אשי allows it, so the בכור may be slaughtered on second-hand testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbade
Permits
An אמורא who forbids here
An אמורא who permits here

phrases.english: Rav Asi forbids,
and Rav Ashi permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַסִּי אָסַר, וְרַב אָשֵׁי שָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two opinions on the question
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אסי: hearsay is invalid for a בכור. רב אשי: hearsay is valid for a בכור.

steps.title: Challenge from the school of מנשה
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי quotes a ברייתא saying hearsay is valid only for the testimony of a woman. That seems to exclude a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said to רב אשי: But the school of מנשה taught that a witness repeating another witness is valid only for the testimony of a woman!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי attacks רב אשי's lenient view with a ברייתא. The word 'only' seems to leave no room for a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows hearsay only in one case: testimony that a woman's husband died, so she may remarry. If that is the only exception, then hearsay should not work for a בכור, which supports רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (introduces a source used to challenge)
From the school of מנשה, a ברייתא from his study hall
Testimony about a woman, meaning testimony that her husband died
Valid, acceptable

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַסִּי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said to Rav Ashi:
But the school of Menashe taught:
a witness from the mouth of a witness is not valid
except for the testimony of a woman!
phrases.notes: This means testimony that her husband died, so she is free to remarry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's lenient opinion
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's view that hearsay is valid for a בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says hearsay is valid only for a woman's testimony, which seems to exclude every other case, including a בכור

steps.title: Reread the ברייתא: wherever a woman can testify
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says to read the ברייתא differently: hearsay is valid in any testimony where a woman is a valid witness. A woman may testify about a בכור, so hearsay works there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read it like this: only for testimony in which a woman is a valid witness.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers by changing how the ברייתא reads. It is not about testimony concerning a woman; it is about testimony a woman is allowed to give.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the new wording, the ברייתא names a whole group of cases, every testimony that a woman may give, and not just one case. A בכור's blemish is one of those cases, so hearsay is valid for it and רב אשי's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach it, read it this way (introduces a new reading of the text)
That a woman is valid for it, meaning she may testify in it
Only

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings use the word 'woman', but differently. רב אסי reads it as testimony about a woman; רב אשי reads it as testimony given by a woman.
steps.whyThisMatters: This new reading is what allows the final halacha accepting hearsay for a בכור.

phrases.english: Teach it: only for testimony
for which a woman is valid, alone.
phrases.notes: In other words, wherever a woman may serve as a witness, hearsay may be used too, and that includes a בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אסי's challenge by rereading the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows hearsay only in testimony about a woman's husband dying
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא allows hearsay in any testimony where a woman may testify, including a בכור

steps.title: רב יימר's ruling and מרימר's nickname
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר accepted hearsay for a בכור. מרימר gave him a nickname for it: 'Yeimar who permits firstborns.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר accepted a witness repeating another witness for a בכור. מרימר called him: 'Yeimar, who permits firstborns.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about an actual ruling. רב יימר ruled leniently, and מרימר mocked him with a nickname.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows the question was decided in real cases. מרימר's nickname shows that some did not agree with the lenient ruling, since it allows a בכור to be slaughtered on second-hand testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: Declared valid
Called him, applied this saying to him
Firstborn (Aramaic for בכור)
An אמורא who mocked רב יימר's ruling

phrases.english: Rav Yeimar declared valid
a witness from the mouth of a witness for a firstborn;
Mareimar called him:
"Yeimar who permits firstborns."
phrases.notes: This was a jab: he is the one who lets people slaughter a בכור too easily.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יֵימַר אַכְשַׁר עֵד מִפִּי עֵד בִּבְכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a real ruling that follows רב אשי's lenient view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יימר accepted hearsay for a בכור, and מרימר objected to it

steps.title: Final halacha: hearsay is valid for a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that עד מפי עד is accepted for a בכור, following רב אשי and רב יימר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The halacha is: a witness repeating another witness is valid for testimony about a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling. Hearsay testimony is accepted about a בכור's blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halacha follows the lenient view, even though מרימר mocked it. This fits רב אשי's reading of the ברייתא: a woman may testify about a בכור, so hearsay works there too.

keyTerms.meaning: And the halacha is (introduces the final practical ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: עד מפי עד is valid for a בכור. The reason is that the ברייתא of the school of מנשה, as רב אשי reads it, allows hearsay wherever a woman may testify.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: a witness from the mouth of a witness is valid
for testimony about a firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute in favor of the lenient view
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Hearsay testimony is accepted to establish a בכור's blemish

steps.title: רבי אילעא: Believing someone who says the animal is a firstborn with a natural blemish
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא rules that if no one knew an animal was a בכור, a person who says it is a בכור with a blemish that came by itself is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא says: If people did not know this animal was a בכור, and someone came and said, 'It is a בכור, and its blemish came by itself,' he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי אילעא about believing a person who reports on his own blemished בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only this person's words tell us the animal is a בכור at all. In the same breath, he says the blemish came by itself, which would let it be eaten. רבי אילעא says we accept both parts of his statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Known or established (here: known to be a בכור)
A firstborn animal, which has קדושה and is given to a כהן
Its blemish is with it, meaning it came by itself
Believed; his word is accepted

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ מוּחְזָקִין בּוֹ שֶׁהוּא בְּכוֹר,
phrases.english: If people did not know it to be a firstborn,
and one person came and said that it is a firstborn
and its blemish is with it, he is believed.
phrases.notes: 'Its blemish is with it' means the blemish happened on its own. Nobody made it on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic connected to the בכור discussion: believing the person himself, not a witness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is believed when he says an unknown animal is a בכור whose blemish came by itself.

steps.title: Isn't this already taught by the משנה about the divorced woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אילעא adds, since the משנה about a woman who says she was married and is now divorced already teaches הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי אילעא teaching us? That 'the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted'? We already learned that in a משנה: a woman who says, 'I was a married woman, and I am divorced,' is believed, because the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אילעא's ruling as unnecessary, because a משנה already teaches the same principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases, the only source of the problem is the person's own words. Those same words also give the solution. Since the משנה already teaches this rule for the woman, it seems רבי אילעא adds nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asking what is new)
The mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted
We already learned this (in a משנה)
A married woman

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
That the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted?
We already learned this:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in כתובות כב.

phrases.english: A woman who said, "I was a married woman
and I am divorced," is believed,
because the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבי אילעא's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His ruling seems to repeat the rule of הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר, which a משנה already teaches.

steps.title: The firstborn case is different, yet he is still believed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought the כהן is not believed, since he is forced to say it is a בכור. רבי אילעא teaches that he is believed, because if he had made the blemish himself, he would have made an obvious one.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: there, the woman is believed because she didn't need to say anything at all. But here, the כהן has no way around saying it, since he won't eat holy meat outside. So you might say this is not a real case of 'the mouth that forbade.' רבי אילעא teaches us that he is believed. If the blemish were his doing, he would have made an obvious blemish and just eaten the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אילעא's ruling is needed. The בכור case is weaker than the woman's case, but רבי אילעא shows the person is still believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman could have stayed quiet, so her own words are what forbid her. The כהן cannot stay quiet, because he needs an expert to check the blemish before eating. That makes his statement look forced and suspicious. רבי אילעא's point is that a cheating כהן would have made a blemish everyone can see and skipped the expert, so his story is believable.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (the mistaken first thought)
There is no way to avoid; he has no choice
Holy meat eaten outside its proper place
A blemish that everyone can see

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן is believed even though he had no choice but to say it is a בכור. The reason is that if he were cheating, he would have made an obvious blemish instead, and he would not have needed the expert at all.

phrases.english: You might have said:
It is there [that she is believed],
because if she wanted, she would not have said it.
But here,
where there is no way for him not to say it,
phrases.notes: He can't just keep quiet. He must tell the expert it's a בכור so the blemish gets checked.

phrases.english: since he would not eat holy meat outside,
I would say: this is not a case of "the mouth that forbade,"
so he teaches us [that he is believed],
for if it were because of that,
phrases.notes: 'That' means the worry that he made the blemish himself.

phrases.english: he would have put an obvious blemish on it
and eaten it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9 by showing a real difference between the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: shows the בכור case has a new reason to doubt, which רבי אילעא then overrides.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the כהן is forced to say it is a בכור, his words are not truly 'the mouth that forbade,' so he should not be believed.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is believed, because someone who made a blemish on purpose would have made an obvious one and not needed the expert.

steps.title: The case of the rented donkey
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי challenges רבי אילעא by bringing up a case about a man who rented out a donkey and told the renter not to take the road by the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי asked: How is this different from the man who rented his donkey to a friend? He told him: Don't take the נהר פקוד road, where there is water. Take the נרש road, where there is no water. The renter took the נהר פקוד road anyway, and the donkey died. He came back and said: Yes, I took the נהר פקוד road, but there was no water there.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי starts a challenge against רבי אילעא by telling a story about a rented donkey. This step sets up the case; the next step gives the ruling that makes it a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The renter admits he broke the instructions, but he claims the danger (water) was not there, so he did not cause the death. The question is whether we believe him, and the answer will be compared to the כהן who says the blemish came by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges it; an objection against the previous statement
What is different? Asks why two cases should be treated differently
Rented out
A donkey

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi challenges it:
phrases.notes: He is challenging רבי אילעא's rule that the כהן is believed (Steps 8 and 10).

phrases.english: What is different from that man
who rented a donkey to his friend,
and said to him: Do not go
on the road of Nehar Pekod, where there is water;
phrases.notes: The owner is worried the donkey could drown in the water.

phrases.english: go on the road of Neresh, where there is no water.
He went on the road of Nehar Pekod
and the donkey died.
He came and said to him:
I went on the road of Nehar Pekod,
but there was no water.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי שְׁנָא מֵהָהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רבי אילעא's rule and the reasoning given in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעא's rule that the כהן is believed that the blemish came by itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel case is being set up where a self-serving claim may not be believed, even though the person could have lied more easily.

steps.title: רבא and אביי argue about believing the renter
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the renter is believed because he could have told a better lie. אביי says that argument does not work when the facts can be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Why would he lie? If he wanted to lie, he could have said: I took the נרש road. אביי said: We do not use 'why would he lie' where there are witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: This step finishes the challenge. It gives the argument between רבא and אביי, and the challenge leans on אביי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא uses מה לו לשקר: since the renter could have claimed something better, he is believed. אביי answers that this logic does not work when the truth is known or can be checked, like witnesses knowing there is water on that road. In the same way, since everyone knows כהנים are suspected of making blemishes, maybe the כהן should not be believed either.

keyTerms.meaning: Why would he lie? He could have made a better claim, so we believe the claim he made
Where there are witnesses; where the facts are known or can be checked
We do not say (this reasoning)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not reject 'מה לו לשקר' completely. He only says it does not work where the facts are known, like witnesses who can confirm the water.

phrases.english: And Rava said: Why would he lie?
If he wanted, he could have said:
I went on the road of Neresh.
And Abaye said:
"Why would he lie" in a place of witnesses
we do not say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the donkey case, which completes the challenge started in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning in Step 10 that the כהן would have made an obvious blemish, so he is believed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to אביי, 'he could have lied better' does not help where the facts are known. Since כהנים are known to be suspected of making blemishes, that suspicion should act like witnesses, and the כהן should not be believed.

steps.title: The cases are different: certainty versus suspicion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. On the donkey road, the water is certain. With the בכור, it is only a suspicion that the כהן made the blemish, and with a suspicion we do use 'why would he lie'.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, there is certainly water on that road. Here, is it certain that he put a blemish in the animal? It is only a suspicion. Where there is only a suspicion, we do say 'why would he lie.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing the two cases are not alike, so רבי אילעא's rule stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's rule applies when the facts against the person are certain, like the known water on the נהר פקוד road. With the בכור, nobody knows the כהן did anything; we only suspect כהנים in general. A suspicion is not like witnesses, so 'מה לו לשקר' still works and the כהן is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? Rejects a comparison between two cases
Certain; definitely known
A suspicion or worry, not a known fact

steps.whatToRemember: 'מה לו לשקר' does not work against known facts (like witnesses), but it does work against a mere suspicion. So the כהן is believed that the blemish came by itself.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, there is certainly water;
here, is it certain that he put a blemish in it?
It is only a suspicion,
and where there is a suspicion, we do say
"Why would he lie."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא?! הָתָם וַדַּאי אִיכָּא מַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 11 and 12 by showing a key difference between the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (certain fact versus mere suspicion)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general suspicion of כהנים works like witnesses, so 'מה לו לשקר' should not help the כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: A suspicion is not like witnesses. 'מה לו לשקר' works against a suspicion, so the כהן is believed.

steps.title: The rule is taught in the name of רבי אילעא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא taught this rule without a name. רבא זוטי told him they learn it in the name of רבי אילעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא was sitting and teaching this rule without saying who said it. רבא זוטי said to רבינא: We learn it in the name of רבי אילעא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about who said the rule. רבא זוטי corrects רבינא and gives the rule its author's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing changes in the law here. The point is the source: the rule about believing the כהן belongs to רבי אילעא, as in Step 8, and should not be taught as an unnamed rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or a rule that was learned
Without a man; without naming who said it
We learn it (this way)

phrases.english: Ravina was sitting and saying
this teaching without a name,
Rava Zuti said to Ravina:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אִילְעָא מַתְנִינַן לַהּ.
phrases.english: We learn it in the name of Rabbi Ile'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רָבִינָא וְקָאָמַר לְהַאי שְׁמַעְתָּא בְּלָא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי אילעא's rule, the גמרא makes clear that the rule is his.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that the כהן is believed about a blemish that came by itself should be taught in the name of רבי אילעא.

steps.title: רבי צדוק's firstborn splits its lip
steps.stepSummary: רבי צדוק, a כהן, fed his בכור barley in baskets. While it ate, its lip split. He came to רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי צדוק had a firstborn animal. He put barley for it in baskets. While it was eating, its lip split. He came before רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a כהן whose בכור got a blemish while eating. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The split lip is a blemish, and the only one who knows how it happened is the כהן himself. This is the kind of case where we have to decide whether a כהן is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal
Barley
Its lip split

phrases.english: Rabbi Tzadok had a firstborn animal.
He put barley for it in baskets.
While it was eating, its lip split.
He came before Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story on the same topic of a כהן and a blemish on his בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a כהן's בכור got a blemish while eating, and he goes to ask רבי יהושע.

steps.title: רבי צדוק asks about a חבר versus an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי צדוק asks רבי יהושע whether a learned, careful כהן is treated differently from an unlearned one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did we make a distinction between a חבר and an עם הארץ?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי צדוק asks his question: does it matter that he is a learned, careful person?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since כהנים are suspected of making blemishes, he asks whether that suspicion applies to every כהן or only to unlearned ones. If a חבר is trusted, he could be believed that the lip split by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Did we make a distinction?
A learned person who is careful with מצוות
An unlearned person, not trusted to be careful

phrases.english: He said to him: Did we make a distinction
between a חבר and an עם הארץ?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: כְּלוּם חִילַּקְנוּ בֵּין חָבֵר לְעַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי צדוק now asks his question about the case described in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a learned כהן (חבר) trusted about a blemish on his בכור more than an unlearned כהן (עם הארץ)?

steps.title: רבי יהושע answers: yes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says yes, we do distinguish between a חבר and an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers רבי צדוק's question with a short 'yes.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חבר is treated differently from an עם הארץ. So רבי צדוק, a learned כהן, is trusted that the blemish happened by itself while the animal was eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, a חבר is treated differently from an עם הארץ, so a learned כהן is believed about the blemish.

steps.title: רבי צדוק brings his question to רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי צדוק goes to רבן גמליאל and asks him the same question: do we treat a חבר differently from an עם הארץ?
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבן גמליאל and said to him: Did we distinguish between a חבר and an עם הארץ?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי צדוק takes the question he already asked רבי יהושע and now asks it of רבן גמליאל, the head of the academy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is asked here. The same question from Step 16 goes to a second authority, which sets up a possible clash between the two answers.

keyTerms.meaning: The נשיא and head of the academy at the time
Did we distinguish, did we make a difference
A learned, careful person who can be trusted with הלכה
An unlearned person who is not careful with הלכה

phrases.english: He came before רבן גמליאל,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי צדוק, still asking about his בכור with the split lip.

phrases.english: he said to him:
Did we distinguish between a חבר and an עם הארץ?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing רבי יהושע's yes, רבי צדוק asks the same question of רבן גמליאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a חבר כהן is believed about a בכור's blemish when an עם הארץ is not.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל says no
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל answers that we do not distinguish between a חבר and an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: No.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל gives the opposite answer from רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע said yes in Step 17. Now רבן גמליאל says no, so the two leaders disagree. This disagreement drives the rest of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: No
A special title, higher than רבי, used for the נשיא
He said to him

phrases.english: רבן גמליאל said to him: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18, against רבי יהושע's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No, a חבר and an עם הארץ are treated the same.

steps.title: רבי צדוק points out that רבי יהושע said yes
steps.stepSummary: רבי צדוק challenges רבן גמליאל: but רבי יהושע told me yes!
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But רבי יהושע told me yes!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי צדוק pushes back by telling רבן גמליאל that רבי יהושע gave the opposite answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is not built on a proof text. It is built on another great רב's ruling. Now רבן גמליאל knows that רבי יהושע ruled against him.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, but didn't
Yes

phrases.english: He said to him: But surely
phrases.notes: Some versions read the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean "but."

phrases.english: רבי יהושע told me yes!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר לִי הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבן גמליאל's no from Step 19 using רבי יהושע's yes from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's ruling that there is no difference
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another leading authority, רבי יהושע, ruled that there is a difference.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל says to wait for the scholars
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל tells רבי צדוק to wait until the scholars gather in the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wait until the shield-bearers come into the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל does not answer right away. He sets up a public discussion for when the scholars arrive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a setup line. The matter moves from a private talk to a public one in the בית המדרש, which prepares the confrontation in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Wait
Literally 'shield-bearers'; the scholars who battle in Torah debate
The study hall

phrases.english: He said to him: Wait
until the shield-bearers come up
phrases.notes: "Shield-bearers" is a nickname for the Torah scholars, who fight it out in debate.

phrases.english: to the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְתֵּן עַד שֶׁיַּעֲלוּ בַּעֲלֵי תְרִיסִין לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי צדוק's challenge by putting off the discussion until the scholars gather.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question will be settled publicly in the בית המדרש.

steps.title: The question is asked publicly in the בית המדרש
steps.stepSummary: Once the scholars came in, רבי צדוק stood and asked the question again in front of everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came into the בית המדרש, the questioner stood and asked: Did we really distinguish between a חבר and an עם הארץ?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that everyone is gathered, the same question is asked out loud in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is the same as before. The difference is the setting: now רבי יהושע has to answer in front of רבן גמליאל and all the scholars.

keyTerms.meaning: Once, when
The questioner
Did we at all? Did we really?

phrases.english: Once they entered the study hall,
the questioner stood and asked:
phrases.notes: The questioner is רבי צדוק.

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם חִילַּקְנוּ בֵּין חָבֵר לְעַם הָאָרֶץ?
phrases.english: Did we really distinguish between a חבר and an עם הארץ?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the plan from Step 21 by asking the question publicly.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The same question, now asked in front of all the scholars.

steps.title: רבי יהושע answers no in public
steps.stepSummary: In public, רבי יהושע answers that we do not distinguish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: No.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע now gives the same answer as רבן גמליאל, the opposite of what he told רבי צדוק in private.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17 he said yes. Now, in front of the נשיא, he says no and does not oppose רבן גמליאל's ruling. This sets up רבן גמליאל's confrontation.

keyTerms.meaning: No (another form of לָא)
The great תנא who told רבי צדוק yes in private

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this is a different רבי יהושע. It is the same רבי יהושע who said yes in Step 17; that is exactly why the next step attacks him.

phrases.english: רבי יהושע said to him: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the public question, opposite to his private answer.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל confronts רבי יהושע and makes him stand
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says: but they told me in your name yes! Stand up, and they will testify against you.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: But they told me in your name yes! יהושע, stand on your feet and they will testify against you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל publicly challenges רבי יהושע for saying one thing in private and another in public, and orders him to stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on רבי יהושע's consistency: his private yes was reported. Making him stand while witnesses speak against him turns the challenge into a public rebuke.

keyTerms.meaning: In your name
Stand on your feet
And they will testify against you

phrases.english: רבן גמליאל said to him:
But they told me in your name, yes!

phrases.aramaic: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, עֲמוֹד עַל רַגְלֶיךָ, וְיָעִידוּ בְּךָ.
phrases.english: יהושע, stand on your feet, and they will testify against you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יהושע's public no using the report of his private yes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's public answer of no
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He was reported to have ruled yes, so his public no contradicts his own words.

steps.title: רבי יהושע admits he cannot deny it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע stands and says that since רבי צדוק is alive, he cannot deny having said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע stood on his feet and said: What can I do? If I were alive and he were dead, the living could deny the dead. But now that I am alive and he is alive, how can the living deny the living?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע obeys and stands, then admits that he did say yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He explains that he could only deny it if the one who reported it were no longer alive. Since רבי צדוק is alive and standing there, he cannot contradict him, so he admits it.

keyTerms.meaning: What can I do?
If only, if it were the case that
To deny, to contradict

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: רבי יהושע stood on his feet and said:
What can I do?
If I were alive and he were dead,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי צדוק, the one who reported his ruling.

phrases.english: the living could contradict the dead;
now that I am alive and he is alive,

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ חַי יָכוֹל לְהַכְחִישׁ אֶת הַחַי?
phrases.english: how can the living contradict the living?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיאַךְ חַי יָכוֹל לְהַכְחִישׁ אֶת הַחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבן גמליאל's confrontation by admitting the report is true.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He admits he said yes, since he cannot deny a living witness.

steps.title: The people stop רבן גמליאל's lecture
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל keeps lecturing while רבי יהושע stands, until the people protest and tell the speaker חוצפית to stop, and he stops.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל kept standing and lecturing, and רבי יהושע kept standing on his feet, until all the people grumbled and said to חוצפית the announcer: Stop! And he stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the crowd protesting how רבי יהושע was left standing, and they make the lecture stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל never told רבי יהושע to sit, so he stood the whole lecture. The people saw this as disrespect to רבי יהושע and stopped the lecture by telling the מתורגמן to stop announcing it.

keyTerms.meaning: Lecturing, teaching publicly
They grumbled, murmured in protest
The announcer who repeated the lecture aloud to the crowd
The name of the מתורגמן

steps.whatToRemember: רבי צדוק's question exposed a disagreement: רבי יהושע said a חבר כהן is treated differently, רבן גמליאל said no. רבן גמליאל publicly forced רבי יהושע to admit his ruling and left him standing, until the people protested and stopped the lecture.
steps.confusionAlert: At the end, "עמוד" does not mean "stand up." It means "stop." The people are telling the announcer to stop the lecture.

phrases.english: And רבן גמליאל was standing and lecturing,
and רבי יהושע was standing on his feet,
until all the people grumbled
and said to חוצפית the announcer:
Stop! And he stopped.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁרִינְּנוּ כׇּל הָעָם וְאָמְרוּ לְחוּצְפִּית הַמְתוּרְגְּמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what happened after רבי יהושע's admission: he was left standing, and the people protested.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people stopped רבן גמליאל's lecture in protest over how רבי יהושע was treated.

steps.title: A priest is believed that an expert saw the firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a כהן is believed when he says he showed his בכור to an expert and it was ruled blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A כהן is believed when he says: I showed this firstborn animal to an expert, and it is blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says a כהן is believed when he claims an expert already checked his בכור and found a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished בכור may be eaten outside the Temple, but only after an expert confirms the blemish. The משנה lets us trust the כהן's word that this check already happened, so others may eat from the animal based on what he says.

keyTerms.meaning: Believed, trusted to be taken at his word
A firstborn animal, which is given to a כהן
Has a blemish, a physical defect
I showed it to an expert

phrases.english: MISHNA: The priest is believed to say:
I showed this firstborn
phrases.notes: He means he showed it to an expert who checks blemishes.

phrases.english: and it is blemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמָן הַכֹּהֵן לוֹמַר הֶרְאֵיתִי בְּכוֹר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the story of רבן גמליאל ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן is believed to say an expert saw his בכור and ruled it blemished.

steps.title: A priest is believed that he received the animal already blemished
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: a כהן is believed to say a ישראל gave him this בכור with its blemish already on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A כהן is believed to say, 'A ישראל gave me this firstborn with its blemish already on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב. A כהן is believed when he says the בכור was already blemished when the ישראל handed it to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matters because a כהן might be suspected of making a blemish himself so he can eat the animal. רב says we still believe him when he claims the blemish was there before it came to him.

keyTerms.meaning: With its blemish, already blemished
A regular Jew, not a כהן, who owned the animal and gave it away

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The priest is believed to say
'An Israelite gave me this firstborn
with its blemish.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב נֶאֱמָן הַכֹּהֵן לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related case of a כהן's believability next to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן is believed that a ישראל gave him the בכור already blemished.

steps.title: Why is the priest believed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב trusts the כהן here. This sets up the next step, where the reason is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Priests could be suspected of causing blemishes, so trusting the כהן needs an explanation. The question gets the answer ready.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a כהן is trusted that the animal came to him already blemished.

steps.title: People don't lie about what can easily come out
steps.stepSummary: The reason: people do not lie about a matter that is likely to be revealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any matter that is likely to come out, people do not lie about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: people do not lie about something that can easily be checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone could simply ask the ישראל whether he gave the animal already blemished. Since the lie would be caught so easily, we assume the כהן would not tell it.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter that is likely to be revealed
People do not lie about it

steps.whatToRemember: The key rule of this sugya: מילתא דעבידא לאיגלויי לא משקרי בה אינשי. People do not lie about something that can easily be found out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is used in many places in the תלמוד to decide when a person is trusted, and the rest of this sugya tests how far it reaches.

phrases.english: Any matter that is likely to be revealed,
people do not lie about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל מִילְּתָא דַּעֲבִידָא לְאִיגַּלּוֹיֵי לָא מְשַׁקְּרִי בַּהּ אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A lie that can easily be exposed is not told, so the כהן is trusted.

steps.title: רב אשי finds support in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה already teaches this: the כהן is believed about the expert, and the reason must be that people don't lie about things that can be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We also learned this in the משנה: A כהן is believed to say, 'I showed this firstborn to an expert and it is blemished.' What is the reason? Isn't it because we say that people do not lie about a matter that is likely to come out?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tries to prove רב's rule from our משנה. He says the כהן is believed about the expert because the claim could easily be checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, anyone could ask the expert whether he really saw the animal. רב אשי argues the only reason to trust the כהן there is the same rule, so the משנה supports רב.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this, a sign of a proof from a משנה or ברייתא
Isn't it because…?

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
We too have learned this:
The priest is believed to say
'I showed this firstborn
and it is blemished.'
What is the reason?
Isn't it because we say
any matter that is likely to be revealed,
people do not lie about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's reasoning from step 30 using the משנה in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that people don't lie about what can easily come out.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה, where a כהן is believed that an expert saw the בכור.

steps.title: The משנה has a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: in the משנה the כהן would not eat holy meat outside the Temple, but in רב's case priests are suspected.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the reason is that he would not eat holy meat outside the Temple. But here, since priests are suspected, they are suspected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אשי's proof. The משנה may trust the כהן for a different reason, which does not apply to רב's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no expert saw the animal, it would still be holy, and a כהן would not eat קדשים outside the Temple. So he is trusted in the משנה because of that, not because of the rule about lies that come out. In רב's case, priests are already suspected about blemishes, and that suspicion carries over to this claim too.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy meat eaten outside the Temple area, which is forbidden
They are suspected
There (the case of the משנה) / here (the case of רב)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say רב's rule is wrong. It only says the משנה cannot prove it, because the משנה could rest on a different reason.

phrases.english: There it is
phrases.notes: "There" is our משנה, the case where the כהן says an expert saw the animal.

phrases.english: because he would not eat holy meat outside,
but here,
since they are suspected, they are suspected.
phrases.notes: Priests are already suspected about blemishes, so we can suspect this claim too.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם הוּא דְּקָדָשִׁים בְּחוּץ לָא אָכֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's proof from step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה is rejected, not רב's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be explained by the כהן's unwillingness to eat קדשים outside the Temple, a reason that does not exist in רב's case.

steps.title: רב שיזבי challenges from an agent buying tithed produce
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי brings a case where an agent who is not trusted on מעשר is not believed that he bought from a trusted seller, even though that could be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי objected: If someone tells a person who is not trusted about מעשר, 'Buy for me from someone who is trusted,' or 'from someone who tithes,' the agent is not believed. Why not? Let us say that people do not lie about a matter that is likely to come out!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי attacks רב's rule with a case about מעשר. There, the agent is not believed even though his claim could be checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone could ask the seller whether the agent really bought from him, so the claim is easy to check. If רב's rule were true, the agent should be believed. Since the source says he is not, this seems to go against רב.

any matter that is likely to be revealed,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof was rejected, a new challenge is raised against רב's rule itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that people don't lie about something that can easily come out (step 30).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The agent's claim could easily be checked with the seller, yet the source says he is not believed. That seems to show the rule is not followed.

steps.title: The agent's case is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins answering רב שיזבי's challenge by saying the agent's case is different from רב's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to answer רב שיזבי's question by saying his case about the agent is not a true comparison. This line is only the opening; the actual difference comes in the next words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שיזבי used the agent's case to show that a checkable claim is not always believed. By saying 'שאני התם', the גמרא keeps the rule that people don't lie about things that can be checked. It claims that something special about the agent's case explains why he is not believed there.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. Used when the גמרא separates one case from another.
There. Here it points to the case רב שיזבי brought about the agent.
'It is different there.' A standard opening for an answer that says the case used in a challenge does not really compare.

steps.confusionAlert: 'There' (הָתָם) means רב שיזבי's case about the agent and מעשר, not רב's case. The גמרא is defending רב by setting the agent's case apart.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the agent and מעשר case רב שיזבי just brought. The reason it is different comes next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of רב שיזבי in step 33 by starting to set his case apart from רב's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): the case used in the challenge has a special feature that does not apply to רב's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The agent's case seemed to show that even a claim that can be checked is not believed, which would weaken the reasoning behind רב's ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The agent's case is different, so it does not disprove the rule that people don't lie about things that can be checked. The exact difference is explained next.
